title: Make authenticated relay pushes usable from desktop and headless flows
author: w0F5vYijNonu8kkqLSa_jYY4GIV-Q5HpbxYY525ggm4

events.title: Make authenticated relay pushes usable from desktop and headless flows
events.body:
## Outcome

Turn the existing signed receive-pack path into a normal user workflow without persisting short-lived credentials in repository configuration.

## Implementation

- Add one shared helper that creates the correct owner or delegated-write canonical, timestamp, signature, and authenticated push URL.
- Expose a desktop action that either performs the push or copies an exact one-shot command, with a separate headless command using the same helper.
- Never write the signed password into `.git/config`, shell history instructions, logs, crash reports, or diagnostics.
- Refresh an expired credential once after a clear authentication challenge; do not retry authorization failures indefinitely.
- Distinguish offline source, invalid identity, insufficient role, expired signature, ref-policy denial, and receive-pack failure.
- Remove stale user-facing copy and comments that still say relay push is unavailable.

## Acceptance criteria

- Owner and delegated writers can push from desktop and headless flows.
- Read-only users receive a clear denial before any ref changes.
- Secret-bearing URLs are redacted everywhere and are not persisted.
- Expiry refresh is bounded and never changes the intended remote or refspec.
- Successful pushes trigger the existing integrity re-attestation path.

## Dependencies

Depends on #435.

## Verification

Add helper, UI, redaction, expiry, role, offline-source, and successful-push tests using the receive-pack scenarios from #435.
